BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter, reviewed against the Buyer Negotiation Playbook

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every protective point. Taken together, the drafting would:

- cut our recovery to a fraction of what we expect;
- fold Title into the general regime;
- shield fraud from recourse;
- turn the data room into a blanket defence;
- let us complete without the Bluefen consent, without the Riverlark payout and without funding the bonuses.

Several statements in the Seller's cover update conflict with its own Disclosure Letter. That gives us a strong, fact-based basis to push back.

**We should not accept any Seller position as drafted.** Two points need particular care:
- **20% cap and 18-month claims period:** Both are playbook fallbacks, but each is usable **only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority**. Neither has been given, so we cannot offer, accept or signal acceptance of either.
- **Fraud carve-out:** No one has authority to waive or dilute it.

---

## 1. Financial limitations (Clauses 12.1–12.3, 13)

| Item | Seller | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | Seller has gone straight to our unauthorised fallback |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | 5x higher, and AUD 250k of loss is permanently unrecoverable |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is our fallback, not authorised |

**Reasoning**
- **Thresholds compound.** With a AUD 25k de minimis, every individual claim below AUD 25k is excluded and does not count toward the basket. The AUD 250k basket is then deducted. On a AUD 24m deal, these thresholds could remove a meaningful share of foreseeable claims before the cap is even relevant.
- **Cap.** The 20% figure matches our fallback, but authority to use it has not been given. We should counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. If the team wants to trade toward 20%, it must first obtain Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
- **Claims period.** Counter at 24 months. Do not concede 18 months without written approval.

**Push back:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar). Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m. Claims period 24 months.

---

## 2. Hidden general-regime override (Clause 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims")

The Seller proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."

This is the catch-all override the playbook prohibits. Its effect would be:
- general caps, thresholds and time limits would apply by default to Title, Tax, IP, the specific indemnities (Ironquay), payment obligations (price, debt repayment, bonuses) and covenants;
- any gap in drafting would resolve in the Seller's favour.

**Push back:**
- Delete the override.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply only to **general Warranty Claims**, unless expressly extended.
- Keep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant categories in separate, self-contained regimes.

---

## 3. Fundamental / Title warranties

The Seller wants capacity and title subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." That is not a sufficient reason to change the risk allocation.

Title and capacity go to whether we receive the asset we are paying AUD 24m for. If title fails, a 20% cap would leave us recovering at most AUD 4.8m.

**Push back:** A separate Fundamental regime, comprising:
- a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
- a claims period of at least six years;
- carve-out from the general basket and de minimis;
- carve-out from any buyer-knowledge bar.

---

## 4. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

The Seller applies limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." Read literally, this would cap and time-bar fraud claims and could bar reliance-based misrepresentation claims arising from fraud.

The playbook position is non-negotiable and no one may waive it. Whether such a clause is fully enforceable against fraud under NSW law is beside the point. We must not concede the drafting.

**Push back:**
- Add an express carve-out stating that nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers.
- The carve-out must apply to all caps, baskets, time limits, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable.

---

## 5. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

The Seller relies on two forms of general disclosure:
- **1.1:** everything "contained or referred to" in the data room as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012;
- **1.2:** the Accounts, the statutory registers and publicly searchable records.

This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. "Referred to" widens it further, to documents that may not even be in the data room.

**Push back:**
- Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
- Only specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter qualify the Warranties.
- Each disclosure must be fair: made with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
- No disclosure qualifies Title or capacity, the specific indemnities or the Tax covenant.

**Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admission):** A non-admission statement is common and can stay. We should make clear in the SPA that it does not cut down the effect of disclosed facts on conditions, covenants and indemnities.

---

## 6. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

The Seller's clause bars any claim for matters known to "the Buyer or its advisers," including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is the widest form of the clause:
- it uses constructive knowledge, not actual knowledge;
- it attributes advisers' knowledge to us;
- it penalises us for conducting due diligence.

It would also neutralise the specific indemnities. We know about Ironquay, Bluefen and DD-006 precisely because they are disclosed, and that is why we are seeking indemnities for them.

**Push back:**
- Delete the clause. Warranties are given notwithstanding any investigation by the Buyer.
- Seller knowledge qualifiers should be confined to named Seller knowledge persons, with a reasonable-enquiry standard.
- Buyer knowledge never excuses Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 7. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)

**Conflict between the Seller's documents:** The update says the Bluefen consent is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.

**Why it matters:** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours plus "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." That could let Completion occur on a consent that is conditional, or whose 11.3 conditions remain unmet.

**Push back:**
- Make an effective Bluefen consent a condition precedent. It must be unconditional, or conditional only on Completion.
- Require documentary evidence, before Completion, that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied.
- Delete "satisfied on delivery."
- Upgrade reasonable endeavours to best or all-reasonable endeavours. The Buyer must have the right to review the consent and waive the condition.
- Request DD-002 clause 11.2/11.3 for our own read, so we know exactly what the conditions require.

---

## 8. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7)

Riverlark has about AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003). The facility has change-of-control and discharge provisions (clauses 8.1 and 9.2). The Seller offers a release "following Completion."

This is inconsistent with the debt-free / cash-free basis. Change of control under clause 8.1 may trigger default at the moment of Completion, and we would own a company whose assets remain encumbered.

**Push back:**
- **Payout letter:** a current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, stating the exact amount including interest and breakage.
- **Direct repayment:** the Buyer pays Riverlark directly from Completion funds, with the amount deducted from the price.
- **Security releases at Completion:** signed deeds of release, PPSR discharges or undertaking to discharge, and any mortgage or charge releases delivered at Completion.

A post-completion release is acceptable only with **both** an irrevocable lender undertaking to release on receipt of the payout **and** Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so we do not offer this.

---

## 9. Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow)

The Seller states that the AUD 420,000 in closing bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. The Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms the bonuses are absent from the funds flow. It also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If they are not in the funds flow, the Company pays them after Completion and the cost falls on us in substance. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.

**Push back:** Choose one of two routes:
- add a specific funds-flow line item covering the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding mechanics), deducted from the price; or
- an express Seller-funding obligation, backed by an indemnity outside the general regime.

We should also require confirmation of the on-cost amounts.

---

## 10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)

The existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

The risk goes beyond the payment. It covers ownership of the IP itself, third-party claims and the cost of re-creating or licensing the materials.

On the amount, DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the Seller itself notes, this is not independent verification. We should not assume the amount is correct, and we should not assume it is wrong.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the SOW3 Project Materials. This includes third-party claims, re-work and licensing costs.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.
- Preserve the cure: payment of all SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.
- Seek independent verification of the amount actually outstanding.

---

## 11. DD-006 export / privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)

The Seller's update calls this "not expected to be material." Its own Disclosure Letter (item 6) says the investigation is preliminary and does not establish access, scope or any notification duty.

Our playbook position is neutral. We do **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification obligation or any loss figure, and we should not let the Seller's materiality characterisation into the SPA. The facts are open in both directions.

**Push back:**
- Delete the "not material" characterisation.
- Add covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation, including whether the link was accessed, the actual scope and whether notification is required;
  - give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings before Completion.
- Any notification decision is to be made in consultation with the Buyer.
- Reserve the indemnity position pending the investigation, and do not fix a number either way.

---

## 12. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)

The Seller calls the renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter (item 8) does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. It also says DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together for timing and scope.

Consistent with the playbook, we neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor treat the AUD 330k as Debt or a price deduction.

**Next step:**
- Review DD-008 and DD-011 together.
- Establish timing, termination rights, whether the renewals were committed near signing, accrual status and the business rationale.
- Decide the treatment once the facts are known, whether that is working capital, a specific warranty or no adjustment. Reserve our position in the mark-up.

---

## 13. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller says tax and IP are "settled under the general regime." Under our playbook, both remain **open**. We should not accept that they are resolved, and we should not assume unlimited liability.

**Push back:**
- State expressly that the Tax and IP regimes remain under negotiation.
- Tax and IP sit in separate categories, not under the general cap or threshold by default. This ties back to deleting the override in section 2.

---

## 14. Title evidence (DD-012)

The Seller relies on the Company share register. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) concedes this identifies the source relied on, not verified title.

An internal register is not independent proof.

**Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority:
- a current ASIC company extract;
- share certificates, or confirmation that none exist;
- the share issue and transfer history;
- the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption rights and consents);
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company over the shares;
- a Seller board resolution and evidence of signatory authority.

Title also stays in the Fundamental regime (section 3).

---

## 15. Other points to verify (not accept at face value)

- **Lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only a notification obligation applies. We should read DD-007 ourselves, confirm no change-of-control consent or default is triggered, and add a pre-Completion notification covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says the restriction is on assignment, not a share sale. We should confirm independently that DD-009 contains no change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Limitations:** Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m. De minimis AUD 5k. Tipping basket AUD 50k. 24-month claims period. Do not concede 20% or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft.
2. **Override:** Delete "limitations apply to all Claims." Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and each category stays separate.
3. **Fundamental / Title:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Fraud:** Full carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
5. **Disclosure:** Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete clause 8.3. Any Seller knowledge qualifier uses named persons plus reasonable enquiry.
7. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent. No consent-on-delivery. A stronger endeavours standard.
8. **Riverlark:** Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** Broadened IP indemnity, cure preserved, AUD 180k figure independently verified.
11. **DD-006:** Delete "not material." Preservation, investigation and update covenants. No assumed breach or quantum.
12. **Sandbar:** Investigate. No Debt classification or price deduction for now. Reserve our position.
13. **Tax / IP:** Record as open. Separate regimes, not the general regime.
14. **Title:** Independent evidence package. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** Verify the Seller's characterisations against DD-007 and DD-009.

**Process point:** Our cover note should state that the Seller's package is not accepted as "fair and balanced." We should use the inconsistencies between the update and the Disclosure Letter (Bluefen "addressed," DD-006 "not material," Tax/IP "settled") as leverage. If the team wants to use either the 20% cap or the 18-month fallback, raise it with Amelia Frost first, before anything goes back to the Seller.

- Seller knowledge qualifiers should be confined to named Seller knowledge persons, with a reasonable-enquiry standard.
- Buyer knowledge never excuses Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 7. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)

**Conflict between the Seller's documents:** The update says the Bluefen consent is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.

The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours plus "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." That could let Completion occur on a consent that is conditional, or whose 11.3 conditions remain unmet.

**Push back:**
- Make an effective Bluefen consent a condition precedent. It must be unconditional, or conditional only on Completion.
- Require documentary evidence, before Completion, that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied.
- Delete "satisfied on delivery."
- Upgrade reasonable endeavours to best or all-reasonable endeavours. The Buyer must have the right to review the consent and waive the condition.

## 8. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7)

Riverlark has about AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003). The facility has change-of-control and discharge provisions (clauses 8.1 and 9.2). The Seller offers a release "following Completion."

This is inconsistent with the debt-free / cash-free basis. Change of control under clause 8.1 may trigger default at the moment of Completion, and we would own a company whose assets remain encumbered.

**Push back:**
- **Payout letter:** a current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, stating the exact amount including interest and breakage.
- **Direct repayment:** the Buyer pays Riverlark directly from Completion funds, with the amount deducted from the price.
- **Security releases at Completion:** signed deeds of release, PPSR discharges or undertaking to discharge, and any mortgage or charge releases delivered at Completion.

A post-completion release is acceptable only with **both** an irrevocable lender undertaking to release on receipt of the payout **and** Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so we do not offer this.

## 9. Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow)

The Seller states that the AUD 420,000 in closing bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. The Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms the bonuses are absent from the funds flow. It also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If they are not in the funds flow, the Company pays them after Completion and the cost falls on us in substance. This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits.

**Push back:** Choose one of two routes:
- add a specific funds-flow line item covering the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding mechanics), deducted from the price; or
- an express Seller-funding obligation, backed by an indemnity outside the general regime.

We should also require confirmation of the on-cost amounts.

## 10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)

The existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

The risk goes beyond the payment. It covers ownership of the IP itself, third-party claims and the cost of re-creating or licensing the materials.

On the amount, DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the Seller itself notes, this is not independent verification. We should not assume the amount is correct, and we should not assume it is wrong.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the SOW3 Project Materials. This includes third-party claims, re-work and licensing costs.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.
- Preserve the cure: payment of all SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.
- Seek independent verification of the amount actually outstanding.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Limitations:** Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m. De minimis AUD 5k. Tipping basket AUD 50k. 24-month claims period. Do not concede 20% or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft.
2. **Override:** Delete "limitations apply to all Claims." Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and each category stays separate.
3. **Fundamental / Title:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Fraud:** Full carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
5. **Disclosure:** Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete clause 8.3. Any Seller knowledge qualifier uses named persons plus reasonable enquiry.
7. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent. No consent-on-delivery. A stronger endeavours standard.
8. **Riverlark:** Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** Broadened IP indemnity, cure preserved, AUD 180k figure independently verified.
11. **DD-006:** Delete "not material." Preservation, investigation and update covenants. No assumed breach or quantum.
12. **Sandbar:** Investigate. No Debt classification or price deduction for now. Reserve our position.
13. **Tax / IP:** Record as open. Separate regimes, not the general regime.
14. **Title:** Independent evidence package. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** Verify the Seller's characterisations against DD-007 and DD-009.

**Process point:** Our cover note should state that the Seller's package is not accepted as "fair and balanced." We should use the inconsistencies between the update and the Disclosure Letter (Bluefen "addressed," DD-006 "not material," Tax/IP "settled") as leverage. If the team wants to use either the 20% cap or the 18-month fallback, raise it with Amelia Frost first, before anything goes back to the Seller.
